title: The Jacobson radical of a w-contractible ring is henselian
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring such that $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal], and let $J=\bigcap_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{MaxSpec}R}\mathfrak m$. Then $(R,J)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Explicitly, for every finite $R$-algebra $B$, reduction induces a bijection between the idempotents of $B$ and the idempotents of $B/JB$. The zero ring is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.2: W is its henselization along its reduced closed-point scheme; hence the resulting affine pair is henselian. This node records only the henselian-pair consequence.

proof.text: Put J = jacobson of zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] to obtain an essentially small filtered diagram of etale R-algebras trivial modulo J and a colimit eta : R → H, with (H,JH) henselian and R/J → H/JH bijective. The vertex is in the universe of R. Reindex by a small model of the diagram to obtain the ind-etale predicate [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

Flatness is [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-flat-quotients]. For each maximal ideal m of R, J is contained in m. Invert the quotient isomorphism to construct H → H/JH ≃ R/J → R/m. This map composed with eta is the quotient map R → R/m, so it kills mH. Since R/m is nonzero, mH is proper. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] to conclude faithful flatness. This argument also covers R = 0: there are no maximal ideals to test.

The existing source class IsWContractibleRing [sk-def-pe-wlocal] already packages the geometric hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-existing-wcontractible-indetale-retraction], including IsWLocalRing as a superclass. Apply its retraction theorem to H to get rho : H → R with rho eta = id. No additional comparison of w-locality definitions is needed in Lean.

Descend the simple-root condition of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] along rho. Given a monic f over R and a0 with f(a0) in J and invertible derivative modulo J, map f and a0 into H. Polynomial evaluation and derivative commute with ring maps. The induced quotient map sends the given unit to a unit modulo JH. Henselianity of H gives a root a congruent to eta(a0) modulo JH. Then rho(a) is a root of f, because f mapped by eta then rho is f. Moreover rho(JH) = J by Ideal.map_map and rho eta = id, so rho(a) - a0 belongs to J. The other field of HenselianRing is J ≤ jacobson of zero, reflexivity here. This is the proved private helper henselian_of_retraction.

Install the resulting HenselianRing R J. Every module-finite R-algebra B is integral over R. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-integral-idempotent-lifting], which is already proved and permits arbitrary universes and the zero ring, to get the unique lift of every idempotent of B/JB. Pair this clause with the henselian structure from the preceding step.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0A02, 0AGU and 09XI, with proetale.tex Tag 0982: retain the pair-henselization and retraction route, descend simple roots directly along the retraction, and use the existing integral-algebra idempotent lifting theorem.

lean.statement: theorem wcontractible_jacobson_henselian (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsWContractibleRing R] : HenselianRing R (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R)) ∧ ∀ (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Module.Finite R B] (e₀ : B ⧸ (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R)).map (algebraMap R B)), IsIdempotentElem e₀ → ∃! e : B, IsIdempotentElem e ∧ Ideal.Quotient.mk ((Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R)).map (algebraMap R B)) e = e₀
